summary: James Miller is a scholar in sinology and religious studies. He earned an M.A. from the University of Cambridge (-1997) and a Ph.D. from Boston University (-2000), and served as Professor at Queen's University at Kingston (attested 2014).
James Morison was an Indology scholar who studied under Georg Bühler. He served as Librarian at the Indian Institute, University of Oxford (attested 1917–1920).

James Murdoch worked in Japanology and history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Aberdeen (~1875–1879) and under Theodor Benfey (~1878–1879), and held posts at the University of Tokyo (~1898–1900), Kanazawa University (~1901–1908), and Kagoshima University (~1908–1917).

James Prinsep worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and linguistics. He served at the India Government Mint in Kolkata (1819; 1830–1838) and the Benares Mint (~1820–1830), and led the Asiatic Society from 1832 to 1838.

James Rennell was an expert in history and archaeology. He served in the Bengal Engineer Group (1764) and worked as a surveyor for the East India Company from 1764 to 1777, later founding the Royal Geographical Society in 1830.

James Robert Ballantyne specialized in Indology and philosophy. He studied at the University of Edinburgh and under James Michael and Francis Johnson, later serving at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University (1841; 1845–1861) and as librarian for the India Office (~1861–1864).

James Robson is a scholar of Buddhist studies, religious studies, and sinology. He studied at UC Santa Barbara and Stanford University, and held faculty positions at Williams College, the University of Michigan, and Harvard University, later directing the Harvard-Yenching Institute.

James Santucci is a scholar of religious studies and Indology. He held appointments at California State University (attested 1998) and served as Chair and Professor of Comparative Religion at California State University, Fullerton (attested 2007).

James Smith Reid was a historian and archaeologist. After studying at the University of Cambridge (~1865–1869), he held positions at Christ's College (1869–1880), Pembroke College (1873–1885), and Gonville and Caius College (1878–1926).

James Sutherland Cotton specialized in history, archaeology, and Indology. Educated at Brighton College, Winchester College, and Trinity College, Oxford, he held posts at Queens' College, Cambridge, and The Queen's College, Oxford (both 1871–1874).

James Tod worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the Royal Military Academy, Woolwich (~1798–1799) and under Yati Gyan Chandra (~1812–1822), serving with the East India Company (~1799–1822) and the Royal Asiatic Society (~1823–1835).
James W. Benson is an Indologist who held an Assistant Professorship in Sanskrit at Harvard University (attested 1999–2003) and a post at Wolfson College, Oxford (attested 2004).

James W. Heisig works in philosophy, religious studies, and Japanology. Educated at Divine Word College, Loyola University Chicago, Notre Dame, and Cambridge, he was a longtime Permanent Research Fellow at the Nanzan Institute for Religion and Culture (1976; 1978; 1991–2001).
James Ward was a philosopher who studied at Fitzwilliam College and Trinity College, Cambridge (~1872–1874). He held an academic post at the University of Cambridge from circa 1897 to 1925.
James Whitehill is a scholar of religious and Buddhist studies who founded the Columbia Zen Center. He served as Professor of Religion at Stephens College (attested 2000).

James Wilson Bright specialized in linguistics. After studying at Lafayette College (~1873–1877) and Johns Hopkins University (~1879–1882), he taught at Cornell (~1885) and held the Caroline Donovan Chair of English at Johns Hopkins from 1905 to 1925.

Jamgön Kongtrul Lodrö Thayé was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under numerous teachers, including Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo, Tekchok Dorje, Chokgyur Dechen Lingpa, and Pema Nyinche Wangpo, and also taught several prominent figures.

Jamie Hubbard is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University and the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Kazuo Okabe and Minoru Kiyota. He held named professorships in Buddhist, religious, and East Asian studies at Smith College (attested 2016, 2026).
Jampa Lhundup works in Tibetology and linguistics. He studied at and holds a faculty post as Assistant Professor of Art History at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (attested 2026).

Jampa Losang Panglung worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Sera Monastery (-1958) and the University of Munich (~1968–1979), later serving as a research staff member at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities (~1980–2004).
